text:
Ian: Drafting a concise drill + runbook for spot GPU pools (focus: warm-pools per-AZ, preflight, canary reroute percentages).

Ian: Goal: validate graceful drain, fallback routing, and cost tagging with a short monthly dry-run.

Maya: Love it. Can we codify a small warm pool per AZ? e.g., warm_per_az=1-2 to avoid cold-start tail.

Raj: Yes. Recommend warm_per_az=2 for prod-critical routes, 1 for low-priority. Keeps p95 tail low for <5% additional cost.

Kim: Suggest a short preflight checklist we can run before the drill. Quick items only.

Ian: Added preflight checklist draft below.

Maya: Also want a canary reroute strategy: start 20% -> 50% -> 100% if metrics look good, with 30s evaluation windows.

Raj: And predictive preempt routing: if cloud webhook sends preempt_score >= 0.65 and ETA < 110s, begin 30% preemptive reroute immediately.

Kim: Ops commands for the drill (copyable):
```
# mark node preempting and cordon
kubectl label node gpu-az2-07 preempting=true --overwrite
kubectl cordon gpu-az2-07

# soft-drain: allow short-lived pods to finish (grace window)
kubectl drain gpu-az2-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=10 --timeout=15s || true

# force-kill any lingering inference pods
kubectl get pods -l pool=spot-az2 -o name | xargs -r kubectl delete --grace-period=3

# trigger canary reroute (internal tool)
./tools/reroute --pool spot-az2 --to reserved-az2 --percent 20 --check-metrics ephem.fallback.latency.p95:<=300
```

Ian: Preflight checklist (drill):
- reserved pool >= min_reserved_capacity (check via dashboard)
- warm_per_az verified and instances show healthy
- circuit breakers configured on routes and healthy endpoints
- KV persistent store reachable and latency < 50ms
- smoke test one model route (3 runs) success
- billing tags configured: fallback_route, pool_from, failover_reason

Maya: Default knobs to include in runbook:
- graceful_window=10s
- kv_persist_window=6s
- canary_steps=[20,50,100]
- predictive_threshold=0.65
- warm_per_az defaults (prod=2, staging=1)

SRE-Oncall: Ops-bot alert format (example):
Ops-Bot: ALERT: 2026-05-12T14:08:09Z - Preempt notice - region=us-east1 pool=spot-az1 nodes=2 eta=102s EventID=preempt-20260512-1408

SRE-Oncall: ack. Will kick off canary reroute 20% and enable model-shard fallback. Notifying runtime-oncall.

Raj: Escalation summary (short):
- auto: system begins canary reroute per policy
- page infra-sre if affected_nodes >=2 OR affected_traffic_pct >=4%
- page eng-runtime if p95 fallback latency > 350ms for >6m
- page product+finance if fallback cost delta > $400/hr sustained 30m

Maya: Post-drill metrics we should capture:
- ephem.preempt.count
- ephem.fallback.latency.p95
- ephem.requeue.rate
- reserved.warm_utilization
- cost.delta.hr

Kim: Telemetry / tagging notes: add labels on fallback spans/traces: preempt_event_id, fallback_route=[reserved|az-fallback|quantized], pool_from.

Ian: Post-incident actions (if triggered by drill or real event):
- quick RCA if >2 nodes or >5% traffic affected
- update knobs: graceful_window +/- 2s, warm_per_az adjust
- schedule follow-up runbook update and small pager drill

Maya: Proposed monthly drill cadence: first Wed 09:30 PT, simulate 1-node and 2-node AZ blips. Rotate regions each month.

Raj: Ops tip: prefer tiny warm pools in each AZ rather than a single warm region to reduce inter-AZ failover costs and latency.

Ian: I'll convert this thread into ephemeral-spot-drill-v0.1 and add links to runbooks index. Who can help run the first drill next Wed?

Maya: I'll run it.
Kim: I'll prepare the webhook simulator and verify telemetry.
SRE-Oncall: I'll simulate the alert and watch dashboards.

Ian: Thanks. After the drill we'll collect metrics and update the cost dashboard, then iterate on canary step sizes if needed.
